title: Dimensions and columns
note: m rows × n columns: n input entries, m output entries. Entry aᵢⱼ: row i, column j. Coordinate-vector images are the columns.

title: Composition
note: Rightmost acts first. Inner dimensions must match. AB and BA can differ. Identity I leaves every compatible vector unchanged.

title: Two-by-two product
note: Each output entry combines one row of the left matrix with one column of the right matrix.

title: Solution-preserving operations
note: Operate on whole equations, including right-hand sides. Keep the other row in a row replacement. Each operation is reversible.

title: Elimination and solution sets
note: 0 = 0 adds no condition. Keep the remaining equations. Back-substitute when each unknown is fixed; otherwise describe allowed free parameters. Verify against the originals.

title: A complete parameter family
note: t ranges over all real numbers. Check both directions: every parameter gives a solution; every solution has such a parameter. Sample pairs alone do not prove completeness.

title: Determinant and inverse
note: Inverse formula requires Δ ≠ 0. Then every target has exactly one input. Check AA⁻¹ = A⁻¹A = I. With Δ = 0, inspect the target: no solution or infinitely many.

title: Area and orientation in the plane
note: Same perpendicular, equal-scale coordinates. Positive Δ preserves orientation; negative reverses it; zero collapses area. Area scale does not specify length or angle changes.

title: Residuals and their limits
note: Every entry zero: candidate satisfies these equations. This does not prove uniqueness. A failed candidate does not prove inconsistency. Small residual need not mean small input error.

title: Transparent Python check
code:
def residual2(m, v, target):
    first = m[0]*v[0] + m[1]*v[1]
    second = m[2]*v[0] + m[3]*v[1]
    return [first-target[0], second-target[1]]

r = residual2([1, 2, 0, 1], [1, 2], [5, 2])
ok = r[0] == 0 and r[1] == 0
print(r, ok)  # [0, 0] True
note: m = [a,b,c,d] in row order; v and target have two entries. Modest finite numeric inputs only. Exact zero suits these integer cases; inspect floating-point discrepancies in context. Predict, use revealing cases, restart and rerun.
